events.title: HMS Beagle Departs on Darwin's Voyage
events.description: After earlier delays and a false start, HMS Beagle set sail from Plymouth, England, on its second survey expedition under Captain Robert FitzRoy, with the young naturalist Charles Darwin aboard.
events.significance: The five-year voyage gave Darwin the observations of geology, fossils, and wildlife, especially in the Galapagos Islands, that led to his theory of evolution by natural selection and the 1859 publication of On the Origin of Species.

events.title: Birth of Johannes Kepler
events.description: Johannes Kepler was born in the Free Imperial City of Weil der Stadt in the Holy Roman Empire. He became a mathematician and astronomer who worked with Tycho Brahe's observational data.
events.significance: Kepler formulated the three laws of planetary motion, which described the elliptical orbits of planets and later provided a foundation for Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation.

events.title: Founding of the IMF and World Bank
events.description: The Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, agreed at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference, came into force after 29 countries ratified them.
events.significance: These institutions became pillars of the postwar international financial system, shaping global monetary cooperation, reconstruction, and development lending for decades.

events.title: Netherlands Transfers Sovereignty to Indonesia
events.description: After a four-year independence struggle and negotiations at the Round Table Conference in The Hague, the Netherlands formally recognized Indonesian sovereignty in a ceremony in Amsterdam.
events.significance: The transfer ended centuries of Dutch colonial rule in the East Indies and marked a major milestone in the postwar wave of decolonization in Asia.

events.title: Soviet Forces Storm Kabul Palace and Install Babrak Karmal
events.description: Soviet special forces stormed Tajbeg Palace in Kabul, killing Afghan President Hafizullah Amin, and the Soviets installed Babrak Karmal as the new leader during the early stage of their invasion of Afghanistan.
events.significance: The operation escalated the Soviet-Afghan War, which lasted nearly a decade, strained Cold War relations, and contributed to the later decline of the Soviet Union and the rise of militant movements in the region.
